name: The Vagabond Club, Singapore, a Tribute Portfolio Hotel
short_description: An intimate Tribute Portfolio boutique hotel in a 1950s Art Deco building near Kampong Glam and Little India.
ai_summary: The Vagabond Club, Singapore, a Tribute Portfolio Hotel is a small boutique property on Syed Alwi Road, within walking distance of Kampong Glam and Little India, occupying a 1950s Art Deco building reworked by designer Jacques Garcia -- his first project in Asia. The look leans into Parisian opulence and vintage glamour, with red velvet interiors, curated art, and The Salon hosting live jazz several nights a week alongside a whiskey library serving Indian-inflected dishes. On TripAdvisor it sits in the upper third of Singapore's roughly 380 hotels, and reviews consistently highlight the bold, unconventional design as the property's defining strength, alongside friendly and professional service and at least one detailed account of repeated elite recognition over an extended stay. As a compact lifestyle hotel, it fits travelers drawn to design and atmosphere over resort-style amenities, and its Jalan Besar-area location suits those prioritizing heritage neighborhoods over Orchard Road or Marina Bay proximity. The clearest recurring watchouts are structural rather than service-related: there is no pool, breakfast is limited to two items per order, some reviews mention waiting for check-in during busy periods, and the hotel isn't directly connected to an MRT station even though two lines are within walking distance.

faqs.question: Does The Vagabond Club, Singapore have a pool?
faqs.answer: No -- as a compact boutique hotel built into a converted 1950s Art Deco building, it does not have a pool. Guests who prioritize resort-style amenities may prefer a larger full-service hotel elsewhere in the city.

faqs.question: How close is The Vagabond Club to Little India and Kampong Glam?
faqs.answer: It's within easy walking distance of both -- the hotel sits on Syed Alwi Road in the Jalan Besar area, bordering Little India and Kampong Glam, though it isn't directly connected to an MRT station.

reviews.title: We review The Vagabond Club, an edgy, art and design-rich haven in Singapore's Little India
reviews.author: Michael Cullen
reviews.summary: Calls the Jacques Garcia-designed boutique an ideal, characterful base and a refreshing alternative to Singapore's conventional hotels, with the whisky bar a standout.

reviews.title: The Vagabond Club Singapore: Small Hotel, Big Personality, Very Little Beige
reviews.summary: Praises the bold design and location between Little India and Kampong Glam; rooms are compact with few facilities but the property wins on personality over standard luxury.

reviews.title: [Hotel Review] Vagabond Club Singapore
reviews.author: Lucas
reviews.summary: Liked the art-forward design and the food, especially breakfast and evening canapes, but was frustrated by fiddly in-room tech such as a non-swivel TV and awkward HDMI setup.

reviews.title: Review: The Vagabond Club, Singapore, A Tribute Portfolio Hotel
reviews.author: Jean-Maximilien Voisine
reviews.summary: Rates the boutique property good value for Marriott Bonvoy members, praising its striking design and location, but frames it as a romantic couples' stay rather than family-friendly.

reviews.title: Hotel Review: The Vagabond Club, A Tribute Portfolio Hotel, Singapore (Art Executive Club Suite)
reviews.author: Mark Chua
reviews.summary: Admires the hotel's distinctive art and unconventional design, noting boutique stays like this suit travelers chasing novelty more than those wanting conventional comfort.
